_readme: CO-OP ECO SERVER — players play alien, Si_RTS_AI runs their economy.
The military layer issues NO orders and builds NO producers. It still runs
its analysis and logs it, because DrMuck asked to keep the intel while the
military approach is rebuilt: 'Can you disable all military related stuff...
But we can log the military layers so to gain more intel.'
The previous soak configuration is saved as rtsai.soak-military.backup.json.
SANITY CHECK BEFORE A PLAYED ROUND — testMode is now FALSE. Left on it would
auto-join a fake client, force-end the round at 40 minutes and restart the
map underneath the players. It is the single most damaging line to leave set
from a soak config, and it is the reason this file is rewritten rather than
_notASoak: Every harness setting is off. These only ever made sense for unattended runs.
testMode false        — no fake client, no force-end, no map restart.
suppressCombat false  — players must be able to shoot. This is gated on
testMode anyway, but it is stated rather than implied.
configCycle off       — one configuration, not rotating arms.
storageBufferCaches 0 — no measurement scaffolding parked next to the Nest.
_storageBuffer: Free Bio Caches parked next to the Nest so the bank stops clipping at the
storage cap. Team capacity is ~4000 per Bio Cache, so an economy earning
300+/s fills it and the game then DISCARDS everything further earned --
cumulIncome under-reports and the eco looks worse than it was.
Raises the ceiling rather than draining the bank, which is why
autoResourceDrain stays false: that one destroyed the money and credited
it back, so the headline number was never cash the AI actually had.
100 caches is about +400k capacity. They sit at the Nest with no patches,
so CapacityForNearestBc reads ~0 there -- they add NO worker capacity and
do not affect the shrimp cap.
_military: OBSERVE ONLY. Deliberately 'enabled: true' with execute and produce OFF,
rather than 'enabled: false'.
enabled:false would switch off the planners too, and with them every line
worth reading — [MISSION] posture and enemy estimates, [BATTALION] what a
force would have been asked to do, [MIL/BP] which ground scores as forward,
[DEFENCE] what ranks as worth holding. Those cost nothing when nothing acts
on them, and they are the intel the rebuild needs.
WHAT IS GUARANTEED OFF, checked in code rather than assumed:
produce:false  MilitaryProduction returns before spending a single credit,
so no Greater Cyst is ever built for military reasons.
execute:false  BattalionManager never calls IssueOrders, and Owns() returns
false for every unit — which matters because two Harmony
prefixes hang off Unit.OnMoveOrder and AIGroup.OnAttackOrder.
With Owns() false they pass every order straight through, so
PLAYER AND VANILLA ORDERS ARE UNTOUCHED. That is the property
that makes this safe for a played co-op round.
blockVanillaAttackOrders:false — belt and braces on the same point. It is
already gated on execute, but a co-op server is the last
place to rely on a second condition.
offence:false  no push posture, so no armed reconnaissance either.
The map layers (enemy_pressure, enemy_value, fow_active, fow_explored) are
written by Perception regardless of any of this — they were never gated on
the military config.
_lockAlienCommander: OFF for player-commanded co-op. The player holds the alien commander
seat and runs the military; the AI runs the economy underneath them.
This only works paired with EcoAssistWithHumanCommander=true in
MelonPreferences -- otherwise the eco planner stands down the moment a
real player takes the seat, and the AI does nothing at all.
Set true for the OTHER co-op mode: the AI holds the seat and commands,
players play as units, and anyone taking the seat is returned to the
field. The two are mutually exclusive.
_eco: The tuned economy, unchanged, except for the node budget.
maxUnbuiltNodes is REMOVED on purpose. It was a flat global 3 and it still
overrides everything if present. Measured 2026-08-09: nodesInFlight was the
most common reason nothing fired at all, with 29k-38k cash idle each time,
node placement gaps reaching 209s against a 9s median, Bio Caches queued
behind it on bcAnchor and shrimps walking to distant patches as a result.
The budget is now per front — maxUnbuiltNodesPerFront x maxNodeFronts, so
3 x 2 = 6. A single chain still stays shallow, because a chain builds one
node at a time and stacking it deeper only freezes cash; two fronts get two
chains' worth instead of sharing one.
_cystQueueMax: Shrimps QUEUED per Cyst, not counting the one already building.
Structure.ProductionQueue excludes the in-progress unit, so 2 here meant
three in the Cyst -- DrMuck: 'third one is added while the one building is
at 1/3 build progress'. 1 = one building plus one waiting, which is what
the code always claimed: no gap when the first finishes, and no third
shrimp's 160 credits frozen two builds ahead.
_openerDoubleCyst: May one opener site take a SECOND Cyst instead of the opening reaching
for another site? A Cyst on ground already reached costs 1500 and no
nodes and no chain time, which is why it wins.
It never built before v0.76.2. AlienConstruction refused it as a stale
duplicate -- the pair lands ~74m apart and the guard radius was 90m. That
guard exists to stop queued placement searches stacking Cysts 20m apart,
so the Cyst radius is now 55m: still well clear of the accidental case,
under the 70m a deliberate pair is planned at.
With this false the opener drops to 3 sites / 3 cysts for 6400 of a 9000
bank and the last site lands at 100s -- measured worse.
_openerTailSeconds: How long the opening's handover RATE is credited for, seconds.
240 (the old fixed value) sits on top of a 240s scoring horizon, so an
opening was scored over an effective 480s -- for a phase that hands off at
3-4 minutes. It is also the term that kept beating the doubled Cyst, and
not on merit: tail = min(rate x T, remaining ore under the Bio Caches), so
a plan with MORE SITES gets a higher cap while a tighter plan with a
NarakaCity layout (1), 2026-08-11. The doubled plan had the best income
(38840 v 36582), best rate (387 v 362), finished first (72s v 114s), used
half the nodes and had the best spread -- and lost by 2617, of which 5736
was tail. It nodes one way; the winner noded north AND south.
120 = credit the handover for the two minutes after handoff, not four.
_remoteSupply: May a Cyst keep producing when its OWN Bio Cache is full, for free worker
capacity elsewhere that the relocator can reach?
Without this, production collapses the moment the blueprint starts adding
sites -- 93% of nominal at 3 producers, 23-30% at 8, with bcCap climbing to
26. Every producer added made it WORSE, because each only ever asked about
Delivery already worked: ShrimpGroupPlanner spills over-capacity shrimps
onto untapped ground and pileUpMaxDetourM is 0, meaning no distance limit.
The producer just never made a surplus to spill.
Measured before enabling: raw=68 transit=68 nearest=446m -- about 60 free
slots team-wide while producers idled, and transit==raw so
pileUpMaxPerPatch never binds. Nearest free capacity was 377-446m though,
roughly 45s of walking, so it is budgeted rather than unconditional.
remoteSupplyMaxWalkS 60 = 540m at 9 m/s. Lower it if shrimps spend too
much of the round walking; set enabled false to restore local-only.
_crowdSoften: GLOBAL crowd softening, 0..1, applied to the beam and every later phase.
0 = the measured curve, unchanged. This is the honest default: the steps
were fitted to observed income, so raising it makes the whole model
optimistic about piling shrimps on one spot.
The opener has its own value below and does not read this one.
_openerCrowdSoften: Fraction of the crowding penalty removed while scoring an OPENING only,
0..1. The beam and every later phase keep the measured curve.
CrowdFactor steps 1.00/0.85/0.70/0.55 at 6/12/18/24 shrimps, so one extra
shrimp can cut a whole site's output 18%. A doubled Cyst pushes its host
over a step, and the surplus that would in reality WALK ELSEWHERE is
modelled as standing there choking the group -- SupplyForecast only frees
shrimps on patch depletion, never on overproduction.
Measured on identical sites and nodes: the doubled plan earned +159 more
income and still lost by 673, because its handoff rate fell 166->162 and
0.5 = half weight. STOPGAP: remove this once the surplus-release source
exists (ECO_OPEN_ITEMS 2b). It compensates for a blind spot, it does not
_coopBlockVanillaUnitOrders: CO-OP ONLY. Refuse move and attack orders raised INSIDE
AICommander.Think on the alien team, so Silica's own commander stops
re-tasking units the players are driving. Player orders arrive from the
network handler, outside that window, and are untouched.
This replaces protection that went away silently: BattalionManager's
move-order block is gated on Owns(), which requires military.execute,
and co-op runs execute:false. Blocking by unit would also be wrong here
-- it cannot tell a player's order from the AI's.
